propositions: The janitor discovery process currently lacks a concern (#12) for oracle strength and contract coverage, leaving weak tests that cannot fail on contract violations undetected (evidenced by bugs 0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e and 9bb7-4430-1202-4d93 escaping in Aug 2026)

Existing rubric at code-review-tests.md defines antipatterns (fail-open oracle, unrealistic fault injection, guards) but runs only on diffs, not on resting trees; concern #12 must extend reach by adding discovery coverage sharded by test-tree region like concern #11

A test-only finding currently anchors prod_impact=none at file path (docs/test-only) rather than at the contract being guarded, allowing weak-oracle findings to sit below impact floor regardless of contract criticality

The janitor must run on repos lacking code-review-tests.md, so concern #12 requires a portable fallback in references/patterns.md with standalone vocabulary (escape_input proof, false-positive floor, three new antipattern ids) rather than re-declaring the rubric

Schema evidence for concern #12 must include contract quote+location, oracle quote+location, escape_input, antipattern_id, and scope; discovery.md:152 hardcodes 'eleven concerns' but concern #12 introduces a version-drift failure mode that nothing presently detects

A durable executable oracle (test_janitor_concern_schema.py) must derive the concern count from both the numbered list and the schema sentence and assert agreement, so adding a future concern without updating the schema fails CI rather than silently drifting
